avoid: Extended entries (price well above EMA-20 at entry) — CONFIRMED LOSER: META entered Jul 15 at ~8.5% above EMA-20, peaked +2.83%, chopped in a week-long digestion range, then broke LOWER and stopped out at -8.04% (-$584.45) Jul 23. The full arc played out exactly as the early caution predicted. Firm rule: treat large above-EMA extension (>~6-8%) as a size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback. PDBC (entered ~6.05% above EMA-20, taken quarter-unit) is the first live test of whether extension-stacked-on-shallow-cross should be skipped outright rather than merely sized down — it is now the tightest-to-stop, watch it.

Shallow EMA cross entries on earnings-adjacent names: TSLA (Jul 7 entry, 0.06% cross spread, earnings Jul 22) lost -4.78% on exit. Rule: SKIP (do not size down) when BOTH shallow cross spread (<0.5%) AND earnings within 14 days apply simultaneously. Live rule under the current trend strategy.

Very shallow golden crosses (<0.1% EMA-20/60 spread): NVDA (0.07%) skipped Jul 15 as a near-clone of the failed TSLA pattern (0.06%). Treat sub-0.1% crosses as noise-level, high reversal risk — skip on sight. BMY at 0.13% cleared this line by a hair, taken at half unit, and is the book leader (+5.99%), validating 0.1% as the skip floor.

Earnings-blackout holds ride to the hard stop with no discretionary exit: CMG (entered Jul 10, earnings blackout Jul 15-29) drifted to its 2xATR stop and filled automatically at -8.06% on Jul 22. The blackout policy working as intended — no death-cross override during blackout means the full 2xATR is the risk. Record of realized blackout downside, not a rule change.

LEGACY intraday RSI buckets (informational, strategy retired): RSI 60-65 0/3, RSI 65-75 0/1, gap-up opens with RSI>60 — all losers historically. Retained only as a record of why the intraday RSI approach was abandoned in favor of trend-following.
